newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court adjourns pro-Kurd party trial until June.
newsitem.headline: Turk court adjourns pro-Kurd party trial until June.

text.p: A Turkish state security court on Friday adjourned until June the trial of leading members of a pro-Kurdish political party charged with having links to separatist rebels.
"The new hearing will be held on June the fourth," judge Orhan Karadeniz told the court room following demands by defence lawyers for acquittal of their clients.

The defendants, including pro-Kurdish People's Democratic Party (HADEP) leader Murat Bozlak, were arrested last June at a party congress where the Turkish flag was torn down and replaced by banners of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
Many of the 47 accused, charged in September, face 22 1/2 years in jail if found guilty.
Pending the verdict, the court has released from custody all of the suspects except the youth accused of draping the PKK flag from the conference hall balcony.

HADEP was formed in 1994 after another Kurdish party was closed by the constitutional court for alleged separatism and 13 of its deputies were expelled from parliament. Six of the MPs were jailed for links with the PKK.
More than 22,000 people have died in the 12-year conflict between the security forces and PKK rebels, fighting for self rule in the mainly Kurdish southeast of the country.
